excerpt: Cloudflare MoQ relays are available through the [Cloudflare dashboard ↗︎](https://dash.cloudflare.com/) and the [API](/api/resources/moq). They are free to use during the beta period.
It provides efficient, low-latency media streaming by leveraging QUIC's multiplexing and connection management capabilities.
Each relay provides an isolated scope — your namespaces, tracks, and objects are separated from those belonging to other relays.
You control who can publish and who can subscribe by issuing tokens scoped to the operations each client needs.
Cloudflare returns a relay ID and two default tokens: one that can publish and subscribe, and one that can only subscribe.
Token secrets are shown once in the response and never stored.
You can also create and manage relays in the Cloudflare dashboard under **Media** > **Realtime** > **MoQ Relay**.
You can create additional tokens and set expiration times using the [API](/api/resources/moq).
Draft-16 requires authentication. Clients send a token in the URL path when opening a MoQ session.
To test against a draft-18 relay in the meantime, refer to [moq-interop-runner ↗︎](https://github.com/englishm/moq-interop-runner).
A user tested the publish demo at moq.dev/publish and called it "buttery as hell. Very impressive." They also noted that South Korea appears on the 'global' CDN map.

Watching the Big Buck Bunny demo (moq.dev/watch/?name=bbb) on a mobile phone showed many horizontal black lines. It played fine on the user's PC on the same Wi-Fi. They asked whether buffer size was the cause and whether it could be tuned client-side or server-side.
A commenter warned that WebTransport, which browser MoQ playback relies on, currently has issues in Firefox (Mozilla bug 1969090). Another user asked whether the demo only works on Chrome.

A user who used to work on a live video platform said MoQ is interesting enough to make them want to work on it again. They asked for senders to be able to publish multiple streams/subgroups, because server-side transcoding adds latency and modern phones can easily encode multiple renditions.
